trades.thesis: Magnite's blowout Q3 (CTV +39%, political ad spend, raised guide) lifted MGNI 21%, but SSP peer PubMatic only rose 2.6% ahead of its own Q3 print on 11-09 after close. Read-through from strong CTV/political demand suggests upside risk to PubMatic's guide; small size because earnings are binary and PUBM's mix differs.

PubMatic is a peer sell-side platform with CTV and political exposure, reports Q3 on 11-09 after close, and has lagged the read-through (+2.6%)

trades.thesis: Intel guided PC market to decline into 2H27 (Client Computing missed by ~$0.7B); Corsair (PC components/peripherals) reports Q3 on Nov 5 and sector sympathy (HPQ -10% premarket) has not hit CRSR yet, which closed flat/up. Expect cautious guide or sympathy selling into earnings. Weakest link: DRAM-kit price inflation may lift Corsair revenue and offset PC unit weakness.

PAGE DATE: 29/10/2026 (published 9:02 PM; the article's metadata lists the same date, 2026-10-29)

Per the page, Intel said it expects the PC market to decline into the second half of 2027. The page calls this significant for Client Computing, Intel's largest division, which sells processors for personal computers.

On causes, the page gives none. It does not explain why the PC market is expected to shrink.

On client segment weakness, the page reports that Client Computing revenue was about $8.1 billion in Q3, against expectations of roughly $8.8 billion, so it missed estimates. It also says

sessions.feedback: Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

summary:
Session 2026-11-16.

Session 2026-11-16. Portfolio stays 100% cash; no trades. Pre-market SPY -0.6%, QQQ -1.2%, so cash is not a drag today. I looked at Telus (TU +19% pre-market on an unsolicited Quebecor bid; BCE +3.5%, RCI no print; antitrust risk, no defensible chain, already priced). Perion (PERI) reported Q3 revenue -18% and withdrew guidance. It is a pending $420M cash deal with Affle, go-shop to 12-11, so it is merger arb with no edge. SMMT fell 15% after the FDA complete response letter on ivonescimab, and HELP fell about 40% on Ph3 data; both are binary biotech with no clean second-order read. MOD +28% on Friday is data-center cooling, and VRT/NVT had already run. NX -19% pre-market has no known cause. CTVA at 9.43 is a spin-off artifact. Macro is odd: 10-year yield 5.13%, PPI 6.5% y/y, Fed hike priced for December, chip rebound unwinding (AMD -9% Friday). Nvidia is in a Huang resignation/China-diversion scandal (Dell and SMCI servers named) and reports 11-17 after close, implied move about 9%. Next session: read the NVDA earnings and Bessent response, and look for lagging peers with a dated catalyst (the PUBM pattern). Also check Telus/Quebecor development for RCI/BCE, what caused NX's drop (and its peers), and Boost/SpaceX tower plays.

NOTES (updated 2026-11-16)
- Tooling: web_search only works via code_execution and returns a JSON STRING (json.loads it; one call per cell; IMPORT json IN EVERY CELL). Benzinga read_page usually FAILS (11-16 too); sec.gov exhibits, stockhouse, seekingalpha, tradingview work via search results. get_quotes/get_history/search_symbols/scan/news work directly.
- Macro regime (Nov 2026): 10y 5.13%, PPI yoy 6.5%, Fed hike in Dec priced 100%, SPY ~754. 11-05 crash (SPY -4.4%, SOXX -12%) then chip 'buying thrust' +17% in 4 days, unwound partly 11-13 (AMD -9%). Nvidia: Jensen Huang resigned 11-12 (China export/Singapore diversion probe; Bessent demands shakeup in 10 days); NVDA earnings 11-17 AMC, implied move 9%. Dell/SMCI servers named in the Shanghai H800/H100 report.
- Day 1 (10-29): Alphabet -13%, ServiceNow -24%, FTNT -20%, SFM -18%. AI-infra names already ran before I looked. Held cash.
- 11-04: STVN -28% (GLP-1 volume headwind); WST sympathy short rejected.
- 11-06: Took small PUBM long (4%) into earnings as slow-diffusion peer; closed 11-13 for +12.5% (+9.9 pts vs SPY). Only trade so far; worked because peer lagged leader and had a dated catalyst.
- 11-16: no trade. Candidates: TU (Quebecor bid, +19% pre, priced), PERI (Affle $420M cash deal, go-shop to 12-11, Q3 rev -18%; merger-arb, idiosyncratic Microsoft/search decline), SMMT (FDA CRL on ivonescimab, -15% pre; read-through to BNTX/Pfizer PD-1xVEGF unclear), HELP (-40% pre on Ph3), MOD +28% (data-center cooling; VRT/NVT already ran), NX -19% pre (unknown cause), CTVA price 9.43 is -90% from high = spin-off artifact, ignore.
- Lesson: By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced. Prefer peers with an upcoming catalyst that have lagged the leader (earnings read-through), or overreactions after multi-day diffusion. Cash is measured against SPY too, and on down days (SPY -0.6% pre) cash is fine.
- Open ideas: NVDA 11-17 earnings read-through (peers with lagged reaction, DELL/SMCI compliance risk); Boost/SpaceX/EchoStar towers CCI/AMT; JBS/China beef quotas; oil/Iran; Telus/Quebecor -> RCI/BCE (watch).

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is weird, second-order research.

Everyone else reads the headline and trades the company in it. You trade the company the headline
does not mention. Start from events in the news and follow the consequences outward: suppliers,
customers, competitors, substitutes, regions, commodities, logistics, weather, regulation, the
odd dependency nobody has priced. A storm hits the region that grows potatoes for a fast-food chain;
which other chain gains, which frozen-food maker loses, which railroad hauls the replacement crop?

- Every new position, long or short, needs a causal chain of at least two steps from the event to
  the company you trade, each step with a source where possible. Code rejects a trade whose ticker
  or company name appears in today's digest headlines, so the link has to be one you found. The
  losers at the end of a chain are as fair game as the winners: short them.
- Borderline delusional is the brief, but the chain still has to be real: each step should be
  something you could defend with evidence. Write down the step most likely to be wrong.
- Spreading across several smaller bets suits this style better than one big one. Small companies
  cost more to trade, so make the expected move worth it.
- Use search_symbols to find the companies at the end of a chain. Read their exposure, do not assume it.
